questions.question: An agent sends a request and gets no reply. What can't it know?
options: Whether the request was lost or only the reply was
questions.explanation: That uncertainty is why resends need idempotent receivers.

questions.question: Why does the planner resend with the same message id instead of a new one?
options: So the receiver can recognise a resend and skip work it already did

questions.question: Without dedupe, billing charged 53 times for 40 jobs. Name one way a double charge happened.
options: Billing charged, the reply was dropped, the planner resent, and billing charged again
questions.explanation: Lost replies cause resends of work that already happened.

questions.question: What does a bounded mailbox force you to decide?
options: Whether a producer waits or gets rejected when the mailbox is full
questions.explanation: Unbounded mailboxes hide that decision until memory or latency blows up.

questions.question: A message crashes its handler every time. What should happen?
options: Retry a few times, then move it to a dead-letter queue so other messages keep flowing
questions.explanation: A poison message must not block or vanish.

questions.question: You move to a message broker with redelivery and dead-letter queues. What do you still have to build?
options: Correlation ids are no longer needed
questions.explanation: Brokers redeliver; only your code can make redelivery safe.
